races.title: State Assembly, District 69
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Josh Lowenthal
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Assembly District 69 (Long Beach and Signal Hill) since December 2022. Former COO and president of FreeConferenceCall.com and general manager at Plum. Earned degrees from Cornell and UC San Diego. Lost a 2018 Assembly race in District 72.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Nurses Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, California Young Democrats and Equality California, per Ballotpedia.
His campaign site lists endorsements from the Democratic Party, California Professional Firefighters, Senator Lena Gonzalez, California Nurses Association, Sierra Club and Mayor Robert Garcia.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions from Lowenthal on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, abortion, gun policy, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored did not load, so his legislation is not covered here. Wikipedia mentions AB 1709 (limiting addictive social media features for minors) but gives no source, so it is not used. Wikipedia also says he owned restaurants, and we could not confirm that from another page. No specific teaching employer or dates were found.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Long Beach, his campaign site says he grew up there and attended public schools, and Ballotpedia says he graduated from Long Beach Polytechnic High and still lives in Long Beach.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the California State Assembly since December 2022. Before that he was COO and president of FreeConferenceCall.com and a general manager at Plum, and Wikipedia and his campaign site also describe him as a teacher and business owner.
qual.why: Prior legislative service of more than three years, combined with a long business-management career, puts him in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.
qual.label: Prior legislative service of more than three years, combined with a long business-management career, puts him in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight to get cities the tools to crack down on residential crime, gun violence and organized retail theft. It also says he will use the state budget surplus to fund housing, mental health and addiction programs for homeless people while dealing with unlawful encampments.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Long Beach, his campaign site says he grew up there and attended public schools, and Ballotpedia says he graduated from Long Beach Polytechnic High and still lives in Long Beach.

cands.name: Carolyn J. Essex
cands.bio: Retired City of Los Angeles employee who spent 18 years as a Policy Analyst in the Community Development Department overseeing Community Development Block Grant funding. Also worked in hospitality operations, as a caregiver, and as a housing coordinator at Hoffman House. Long Beach resident. First-time candidate.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by Intentional Ballot Conversations (Sway voting group by Mary Senegar). She says she has sought endorsements from Democratic clubs, unions and advocacy groups.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Carolyn Essex was born or raised, or when she moved to California. Her survey gives only a 12-year Long Beach residency. We found no stated positions on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police, guns, abortion or school choice. Her survey answers are general: infrastructure, homelessness, seniors, working families and K-12 student protections. We found no record of her taking action on any of these topics, and no record of her taking a stance on development or data centers. Only one endorsement is listed, and she has no prior elected office.

local.label: Roots 40: Her Ballotpedia survey says she is a 12-year resident of Long Beach, and she worked for the City of Los Angeles for 18 years and raised her son in Long Beach's Cambodia Town corridor; her birthplace and upbringing are not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Spent 18 years as a Policy Analyst in the City of Los Angeles Community Development Department overseeing CDBG funding and program accountability. She also worked in hospitality operations, as a caregiver, and as a housing coordinator at a transitional home. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: Her long career as a public-sector policy analyst with grant funding oversight fits law and budget work, but she has no legislative or elected experience, which places her in the middle range.
qual.label: Her long career as a public-sector policy analyst with grant funding oversight fits law and budget work, but she has no legislative or elected experience, which places her in the middle range.
